## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Ucchudāyikāvimānavatthu* (Vv 30), rendered into English as the "Sugarcane Mansion," is a verse text included in the *Vimānavatthu* of the Pali Tipiṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The core teaching of the narrative illustrates that even an ordinary, modest devotional gift—offering a small piece of sugarcane to a monastic—yields immense karmic reward and rebirth in a heavenly mansion endowed with abundant happiness [SuttaCentral]. Six translations across six languages are recorded on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].
In terms of parallels and text reuse, SuttaCentral identifies *Ucchuvimānavatthu* (Vv 48) as a full internal parallel [SuttaCentral]. This relationship is confirmed by DharmaNexus, which detects extensive verbatim text reuse between Vv 30 and Vv 48 over twelve segments (§0.1–12.1) with a similarity score of 0.98 [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records extensive reuse across 40 segments in the commentary, the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. Beyond Pali literature, DharmaNexus detects low-scoring automated alignments with the Chinese "other translation" of the *Saṃyuktāgama* (*Bieyi za ahan jing*, T 100) and two Tibetan Mahāyāna sūtras (D0082 and D0062), though these reflect formulaic phrase overlaps rather than established historical parallels [DharmaNexus].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
